newsitem.title: USA: General Mills backs Q2 EPS estimate.
newsitem.headline: General Mills backs Q2 EPS estimate.

text.p: General Mills Inc Chairman Stephen Sanger said he considers a First Call consensus estimate of $0.95 a share for the fiscal second quarter to be reasonable.
"I think that's a reasonable place for them (analysts) to be. I'm not urging them to change their expectations," Sanger told reporters after the company's annual meeting here Monday.
Sanger also said he expects General Mills, the second largest maker of ready-to-eat breakfast cereals, to post earnings in fiscal 1997 above the $3.00 a share it earned in fiscal 1996.
"General Mills will show renewed earnings growth beginning in the second quarter. We expect to achieve record earnings in (fiscal year) 1997," Sanger said.

Sanger later explained the record is based on the $3.00 a share General Mills earned in fiscal 1996, its full year following the spin-off of its restaurant holdings. The restaurant business was split off at the end of fiscal 1995.
The current First Call consensus earnings estimate for fiscal 1997 is $3.06 a share.

Sanger told shareholders that General Mills expects to close the purchase of the branded cereal and snacks mix business from Ralcorp Holdings Inc within the next few months. After the meeting, Sanger said the deal is not expected to close before January 1, 1997.
"We expect to complete the Ralcorp transaction over the next few months. The process is well underway and we are now responding to FTC (Federal Trade Commission) inquiries," Sanger said.

In August, General Mills said it planned to buy Ralcorp's branded cereal and snack mix business for a total of $570 million, involving an expected $330 million to $360 million in common stock and the assumption of between $210 million and $240 million in Ralcorp debt.

At the meeting, a shareholder proposal in favor of cumulative voting in the election of board members was defeated. The proposal received 34.6 million votes in favor and 78.7 million against, with 10.2 million shares abstaining.
